title: Spell-IT-Out
description: Spell-IT-Out is an EEG dataset recorded from 25 native Italian speakers who listened to sentences, repeated them, and then produced them syllable by syllable at a fixed pace. Production was either overt (spoken aloud) or covert (imagined without movement). Data comprise 61 EEG channels plus one EOG channel sampled at 2048 Hz, with hand-corrected word and syllable timings for overt speech released as events. Derivative preprocessed EEG and syllable epochs for machine learning are also provided.
methods_description: EEG was recorded with a 64-electrode ANT Neuro waveguard cap and eego sports amplifier at 2048 Hz (reference CPz, ground AFz), with an EOG electrode below the left eye, using ROS-Neuro. Each trial comprised fixation, listening to a synthesized sentence, repetition, and paced syllabification, in 3 overt runs followed by 3 covert runs. Overt speech was segmented with Silero-VAD, aligned with the Montreal Forced Aligner, and manually corrected in Praat.
